MONDO:0016755 MONDO:0979660 neuroblastoma-like schwannoma NCIT:C207079 MONDO:equivalentTo Neuroblastoma-Like Schwannoma A rare schwannoma characterized by the presence of large rosette-like structures that are surrounded by small, round, hyperchromatic Schwann cells. MONDO:0002546 MONDO:0979661 hereditary melanoma with cdk4 mutation NCIT:C207624 MONDO:equivalentTo Hereditary Melanoma with CDK4 Mutation A hereditary cutaneous melanoma caused by germline mutation(s) in the CDK4 gene. MONDO:0018961 MONDO:0979662 vulvar cancer by ajcc v9 stage NCIT:C207662 MONDO:equivalentTo Vulvar Cancer by AJCC v9 Stage A term that refers to the staging of vulvar cancer according to the American Joint Committee on Cancer, 9th edition. This staging system applies to carcinomas. It does not apply to sarcomas, hematopoietic neoplasms, melanomas, and Merkel cell carcinomas. (from AJCC 9th Ed.) MONDO:0005215 MONDO:0979663 appendix carcinoma by ajcc v9 stage NCIT:C207705 MONDO:equivalentTo Appendix Carcinoma by AJCC v9 Stage A term that refers to the staging of appendix carcinoma according to the American Joint Committee on Cancer, 9th edition. This staging system applies to adenocarcinomas, mucinous neoplasms (low-grade mucinous neoplasms and high-grade mucinous neoplasms), poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinomas, mixed neuroendocrine-nonneuroendocrine neoplasms (mixed adenocarcinoma-neuroendocrine carcinoma), and goblet cell adenocarcinomas (formerly termed goblet cell carcinoids). Well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors (carcinoids) are staged according to the classification for neuroendocrine tumors of the appendix. (from AJCC 9th Ed.) MONDO:0003196 MONDO:0979664 thyroid-like follicular renal cell carcinoma NCIT:C207787 MONDO:equivalentTo Thyroid-Like Follicular Renal Cell Carcinoma An extremely rare type of renal cell carcinoma that histologically resembles thyroid follicular neoplasms. It is a well-circumscribed mass, characterized by the presence of thyroid-like follicles that contain eosinophilic, colloid-like material. It is negative for thyroid transcription factor 1 (TTF-1) and thyroglobulin. The majority of the reported cases have a low-grade malignant potential. Rare cases with lymph nodes involvement and distant metastases have also been described. MONDO:0005549 MONDO:0979665 anal cancer by ajcc v9 stage NCIT:C207789 MONDO:equivalentTo Anal Cancer by AJCC v9 Stage A term that refers to the staging of anal cancer according to the American Joint Committee on Cancer, 9th edition. This staging system applies to all carcinomas arising in the anal canal, including high-grade neuroendocrine carcinomas (small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma and large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma), carcinomas that arise within anorectal fistulas, and those arising in the perianal area. This staging system does not apply to sarcomas (they are staged according to the classification for soft tissue sarcomas of the abdomen and thoracic visceral organs), mucosal melanomas of the anus (no AJCC staging system), and well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors (no AJCC staging system). Premalignant lesions [i.e., LSIL, HSIL, anal intraepithelial neoplasia (AIN), Paget's disease, Bowen's disease] are not part of the AJCC system. (from AJCC 9th Ed.) MONDO:0003199 MONDO:0979666 refractory secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis NCIT:C207802 MONDO:equivalentTo Refractory Secondary Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis Secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis that is resistant to treatment. MONDO:0979667 duodenal and ampulla of vater neuroendocrine tumor NCIT:C207852 MONDO:equivalentTo Duodenal and Ampulla of Vater Neuroendocrine Tumor A well-differentiated, low-, intermediate-, or high-grade neoplasm with neuroendocrine differentiation that arises from the duodenum or ampulla of Vater. MONDO:0002995 MONDO:0979668 appendix neuroendocrine tumor by ajcc v9 stage NCIT:C207999 MONDO:equivalentTo Appendix Neuroendocrine Tumor by AJCC v9 Stage A term that refers to the staging of appendix neuroendocrine tumors, based on the American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) v9 staging guidelines. This staging system applies only to well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors of the appendix (NET G1, G2, and G3). It does not apply to high-grade neuroendocrine carcinoma (NEC), goblet cell adenocarcinoma, and mixed adenocarcinoma-NET/NEC of the appendix. (from AJCC 9th Ed.) MONDO:0015066 MONDO:0979669 extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma NCIT:C208025 MONDO:equivalentTo Extrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma A cholangiocarcinoma that arises from the extrahepatic bile ducts. It includes hilar (perihilar) cholangiocarcinoma and distal cholangiocarcinoma (distal bile duct adenocarcinoma). MONDO:0002665,MONDO:0019087 MONDO:0979670 jejunal and ileal neuroendocrine tumor NCIT:C208152 MONDO:equivalentTo Jejunal and Ileal Neuroendocrine Tumor A well-differentiated, low-, intermediate-, or high-grade neoplasm with neuroendocrine differentiation that arises from the jejunum or ileum. MONDO:0002995 MONDO:0979671 pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor by ajcc v9 stage NCIT:C208221 MONDO:equivalentTo Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumor by AJCC v9 Stage A term that refers to the staging of pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor, based on the American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) v9 staging guidelines. This staging system applies only to well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors of the pancreas (NET G1, G2, and G3). It does not apply to carcinomas of the pancreas, including poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinoma (NEC) and mixed neuroendocrine non-neuroendocrine (MiNEN) neoplasms of the pancreas. (from AJCC 9th Ed.) MONDO:0019954 MONDO:0979672 cold agglutinin disease NCIT:C208228 MONDO:equivalentTo Cold Agglutinin Disease A rare disorder that manifests with autoimmune hemolytic anemia and is caused by cold-reacting autoantibodies. It may be a primary clonal B-cell lymphoproliferative disorder or a secondary disorder, resulting from infection or malignancy. MONDO:0979673 childhood hematopoietic and lymphatic system neoplasm NCIT:C208293 MONDO:equivalentTo Childhood Hematopoietic and Lymphatic System Neoplasm A benign or malignant (primary or metastatic) neoplasm that affects the hematopoietic and lymphatic system and occurs during childhood. MONDO:0021079,MONDO:0002334 MONDO:0979674 gastric neuroendocrine tumor by ajcc v9 stage NCIT:C208301 MONDO:equivalentTo Gastric Neuroendocrine Tumor by AJCC v9 Stage A term that refers to the staging of gastric neuroendocrine tumors, based on the American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) v9 staging guidelines. This staging system applies only to well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors of the stomach (NET G1, G2, and G3). It does not apply to carcinoma of the stomach including neuroendocrine carcinoma (NEC), mixed adenocarcinoma-NEC and mixed adenocarcinoma-NET. (from AJCC 9th Ed.) MONDO:0015062 MONDO:0979675 childhood who grade 3 glioma NCIT:C208306 MONDO:equivalentTo Childhood WHO Grade 3 Glioma A WHO grade 3 glioma that occurs during childhood. MONDO:1010030,MONDO:0021640 MONDO:0979676 cutaneous blue nevus NCIT:C208328 MONDO:equivalentTo Cutaneous Blue Nevus An intradermal nevus characterized by the presence of benign pigmented dendritic spindle-shaped melanocytes. It most frequently occurs in the skin of the distal upper extremities, followed by the lower extremities, scalp, face, and buttocks. It usually presents as a single blue or blue-black papular lesion that is less than 1cm in diameter. Simple excision is usually curative. MONDO:0006680,MONDO:0006813 MONDO:0979677 childhood melanocytic neoplasm NCIT:C208332 MONDO:equivalentTo Childhood Melanocytic Neoplasm A benign, atypical, or malignant neoplasm that arises from and is composed of melanocytes and occurs during childhood. MONDO:0021143,MONDO:0021079 MONDO:0979678 acute promyelocytic leukemia NCIT:C208352 MONDO:equivalentTo Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia An acute myeloid leukemia characterized by the predominance of abnormal promyelocytes and translocations involving the retinoic acid receptor-α (RARA) gene. Over 95% of cases are characterized by the presence of the reciprocal balanced translocation t(15;17)(q24.1;q21.2) that results in the fusion of the promyelocytic leukemia (PML) gene and RARA gene. The remainder of the cases show variant RARA gene translocations with other genes including NUMA1, ZBTB16, STAT5B, and NPM1. MONDO:0017893 MONDO:0979679 periorbital neoplasm NCIT:C208455 MONDO:equivalentTo Periorbital Neoplasm A benign or malignant neoplasm that affects the periorbital soft tissue. MONDO:0024611 MONDO:0979680 orbital squamous cell carcinoma NCIT:C208484 MONDO:equivalentTo Orbital Squamous Cell Carcinoma A squamous cell carcinoma that affects the orbital region. In the majority of cases, the lesions represent metastatic involvement of the orbital structures by cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma. Primary squamous cell carcinomas in the orbital region are exceedingly rare. MONDO:0010150,MONDO:0002889 MONDO:0979681 tubular adenoma NCIT:C209283 MONDO:equivalentTo Tubular Adenoma An adenoma characterized by the presence of a tubular architectural pattern. The vast majority of cases occur in the gastrointestinal tract. MONDO:0004972 MONDO:0979682 villous adenoma NCIT:C209284 MONDO:equivalentTo Villous Adenoma An adenoma characterized by the presence of a villous architectural pattern. The vast majority of cases occur in the gastrointestinal tract. MONDO:0004972 MONDO:0979683 tubulovillous adenoma NCIT:C209285 MONDO:equivalentTo Tubulovillous Adenoma An adenoma characterized by the presence of a tubular and a villous architectural pattern. The vast majority of cases occur in the gastrointestinal tract. MONDO:0004972 MONDO:0979684 secondary acute myeloid leukemia in acquired aplastic anemia NCIT:C209345 MONDO:equivalentTo Secondary Acute Myeloid Leukemia in Acquired Aplastic Anemia An acute myeloid leukemia developing in patients with a prior history of acquired aplastic anemia. MONDO:0019457 MONDO:0979685 thyroid gland low grade medullary carcinoma NCIT:C210125 MONDO:equivalentTo Thyroid Gland Low Grade Medullary Carcinoma A thyroid gland medullary carcinoma with no necrosis, less than 5 mitoses per 2 mm2, and a Ki-67 index less than 5%. MONDO:0015277 MONDO:0979686 thyroid gland high grade medullary carcinoma NCIT:C210129 MONDO:equivalentTo Thyroid Gland High Grade Medullary Carcinoma A thyroid gland medullary carcinoma with at least one of the following characteristics: necrosis, 5 or more mitoses per 2 mm2, and/or a Ki-67 index equal to or greater than 5%. MONDO:0015277 MONDO:0979687 digestive system adenocarcinoma NCIT:C210140 MONDO:equivalentTo Digestive System Adenocarcinoma An adenocarcinoma that arises from any part of the digestive system. MONDO:0006181,MONDO:0004970 MONDO:0979688 amphicrine carcinoma NCIT:C210709 MONDO:equivalentTo Amphicrine Carcinoma A carcinoma that shows both neuroendocrine and non-neuroendocrine differentiation in the same malignant cells. It has been described in the digestive system and extra-digestive sites. It is distinct from mixed neuroendocrine non-neuroendocrine neoplasms as it does not contain two distinct neoplastic components, one neuroendocrine and one non-neuroendocrine. MONDO:0004993 MONDO:0979689 canine oligodendroglioma NCIT:C210818 MONDO:equivalentTo Canine Oligodendroglioma Oligodendroglioma occurring in a dog. MONDO:0700151 MONDO:0979690 canine astrocytoma NCIT:C210824 MONDO:equivalentTo Canine Astrocytoma Astrocytoma occurring in a dog. MONDO:0700151 MONDO:0979691 nonmetastatic castration-resistant prostate carcinoma NCIT:C210980 MONDO:equivalentTo Nonmetastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Carcinoma A prostate carcinoma that is confined to the prostate gland and shows rising prostate-specific antigen concentration despite castration therapy. It progresses to metastatic disease. MONDO:0850353 MONDO:0979692 metastatic castration-resistant prostate carcinoma NCIT:C210981 MONDO:equivalentTo Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Carcinoma A prostate carcinoma that has spread to other sites and is resistant to castration therapy. MONDO:0004956,MONDO:0850353 MONDO:0979693 bronchial papillomatosis NCIT:C211514 MONDO:equivalentTo Bronchial Papillomatosis Recurrent respiratory papillomatosis that affects the bronchi. MONDO:0018955,MONDO:0021117 MONDO:0979694 tracheal papillomatosis NCIT:C211515 MONDO:equivalentTo Tracheal Papillomatosis Recurrent respiratory papillomatosis that affects the trachea. MONDO:0021210,MONDO:0018955 MONDO:0979695 non-keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma NCIT:C211551 MONDO:equivalentTo Non-Keratinizing Squamous Cell Carcinoma A squamous cell carcinoma composed of malignant cells without morphologic evidence of keratin production. MONDO:0005096 MONDO:0979696 ebv-related nasopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma NCIT:C211843 MONDO:equivalentTo EBV-Related Nasopharyngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma A nasopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma that is caused by Epstein-Barr virus infection. The vast majority of nasopharyngeal non-keratinizing squamous cell carcinomas (differentiated or type II and undifferentiated or type III nasopharyngeal squamous cell carcinomas) and a small minority of nasopharyngeal keratinizing squamous cell carcinomas (type I nasopharyngeal squamous cell carcinomas) are associated with Epstein-Barr virus infection. MONDO:0006060,MONDO:0017344 MONDO:0979697 type ir pleuropulmonary blastoma NCIT:C211861 MONDO:equivalentTo Type Ir Pleuropulmonary Blastoma A subtype of type I pleuropulmonary blastoma characterized by the presence of cysts without the presence of primitive malignant small cells. MONDO:0020555 MONDO:0979698 gastrointestinal stromal tumor with kit gene mutation NCIT:C211871 MONDO:equivalentTo Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor with KIT Gene Mutation A gastrointestinal stromal tumor characterized by the presence of KIT gene mutations. MONDO:0011719 MONDO:0979699 gastrointestinal stromal tumor with pdgfra gene mutation NCIT:C211872 MONDO:equivalentTo Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor with PDGFRA Gene Mutation A gastrointestinal stromal tumor characterized by the presence of PDGFRA gene mutations. MONDO:0011719 MONDO:0979700 succinate dehydrogenase-deficient gastrointestinal stromal tumor NCIT:C211873 MONDO:equivalentTo Succinate Dehydrogenase-Deficient Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor A gastrointestinal stromal tumor characterized by the presence of mutations in the SDH genes and absence of mutations in the KIT and PDGFRA genes. It has an epithelioid morphology and a multinodular growth pattern. MONDO:0011719 MONDO:0979701 central nervous system lymphoma NCIT:C212063 MONDO:equivalentTo Central Nervous System Lymphoma A non-Hodgkin or Hodgkin lymphoma that either arises in the central nervous system or has spread to the central nervous system following the initial presentation in another nodal or extranodal site. MONDO:0017207,MONDO:0003641,MONDO:0002714 MONDO:0979702 conjunctival hereditary benign intraepithelial dyskeratosis NCIT:C212097 MONDO:equivalentTo Conjunctival Hereditary Benign Intraepithelial Dyskeratosis A rare autosomal dominant disorder with high penetrance that affects the limbal conjunctiva. It is almost exclusively encountered in Native Americans belonging to the Haliwa-Saponi tribe of northeastern North Carolina and is caused by a duplication in chromosome 4q35. It is characterized by the presence of frequently bilateral, elevated epithelial dyskeratotic plaques in the limbal conjunctiva. There is prominent inflammation in substantia propria. Epithelial dysplasia is absent. MONDO:0007486,MONDO:0006105 MONDO:0979703 oral mucosa hereditary benign intraepithelial dyskeratosis NCIT:C212098 MONDO:equivalentTo Oral Mucosa Hereditary Benign Intraepithelial Dyskeratosis A rare autosomal dominant disorder with high penetrance that affects the oral mucosa. It is almost exclusively encountered in Native Americans belonging to the Haliwa-Saponi tribe of northeastern North Carolina and is caused by a duplication in chromosome 4q35. It is characterized by the presence of elevated epithelial dyskeratotic plaques in the oral mucosa. Epithelial dysplasia is absent. MONDO:0021445,MONDO:0007486 MONDO:0979704 urticaria pigmentosa/maculopapular cutaneous mastocytosis, monomorphic variant NCIT:C212102 MONDO:equivalentTo Urticaria Pigmentosa/Maculopapular Cutaneous Mastocytosis, Monomorphic Variant A variant of urticaria pigmentosa/maculopapular cutaneous mastocytosis characterized by the presence of multiple small, roundish maculopapular skin lesions. MONDO:0019316 MONDO:0979705 urticaria pigmentosa/maculopapular cutaneous mastocytosis, polymorphic variant NCIT:C212103 MONDO:equivalentTo Urticaria Pigmentosa/Maculopapular Cutaneous Mastocytosis, Polymorphic Variant A variant of urticaria pigmentosa/maculopapular cutaneous mastocytosis characterized by the presence of larger skin lesions of variable size compared to the monomorphic variant. MONDO:0019316 MONDO:0979706 multiple mastocytomas of the skin NCIT:C212107 MONDO:equivalentTo Multiple Mastocytomas of the Skin Multiple distinct mastocytomas that arise from the skin. MONDO:0021048 MONDO:0979707 conjunctival conventional squamous cell carcinoma NCIT:C212110 MONDO:equivalentTo Conjunctival Conventional Squamous Cell Carcinoma A conjunctival squamous cell carcinoma characterized by the presence of various degrees of keratinization. MONDO:0006173 MONDO:0979708 conjunctival basaloid squamous cell carcinoma NCIT:C212111 MONDO:equivalentTo Conjunctival Basaloid Squamous Cell Carcinoma A conjunctival poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma characterized by the presence of malignant cells with scant basophilic cytoplasm, a high nuclear to cytoplasmic ratio, and oval to spindle hyperchromatic nuclei without prominent nucleoli. Apoptosis and tumor cell necrosis are present. MONDO:0003486,MONDO:0006173 MONDO:0979709 conjunctival squamous cell carcinoma with mucinous differentiation NCIT:C212112 MONDO:equivalentTo Conjunctival Squamous Cell Carcinoma with Mucinous Differentiation A conjunctival squamous cell carcinoma characterized by the presence of focal intracytoplasmic mucin. MONDO:0006173 MONDO:0979710 conjunctival acantholytic squamous cell carcinoma NCIT:C212113 MONDO:equivalentTo Conjunctival Acantholytic Squamous Cell Carcinoma A conjunctival squamous cell carcinoma characterized by the presence of acantholysis of the tumor cells that results in the formation of pseudolumina resembling glandular structures. MONDO:0006173,MONDO:0003487 MONDO:0979711 conjunctival pigmented squamous cell carcinoma NCIT:C212114 MONDO:equivalentTo Conjunctival Pigmented Squamous Cell Carcinoma A conjunctival squamous cell carcinoma that occurs in patients with Fitzpatrick skin types IV-VI and is characterized by the presence of dendritic melanocytic hyperplasia among the tumor cells. MONDO:0006173 MONDO:0979712 malignant histiocytic and dendritic cell neoplasm NCIT:C212210 MONDO:equivalentTo Malignant Histiocytic and Dendritic Cell Neoplasm A hematopoietic and lymphoid tissue neoplasm that arises from histiocytic and dendritic cells and is characterized by malignant cytological and architectural features, and presence of invasive features or metastatic potential. This category includes histiocytic sarcoma, fibroblastic reticular cell sarcoma, follicular dendritic cell sarcoma, interdigitating dendritic cell sarcoma, Langerhans cell sarcoma, and plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm. MONDO:0004992,MONDO:0006247 MONDO:0979713 pigmented conjunctival squamous intraepithelial neoplasia NCIT:C212836 MONDO:equivalentTo Pigmented Conjunctival Squamous Intraepithelial Neoplasia A conjunctival squamous intraepithelial neoplasia that occurs in patients with Fitzpatrick skin types IV-VI and is characterized by the presence of dendritic melanocytic hyperplasia among the dysplastic cells. MONDO:0003453 MONDO:0979714 conjunctival squamous intraepithelial neoplasia with mucinous differentiation NCIT:C212841 MONDO:equivalentTo Conjunctival Squamous Intraepithelial Neoplasia with Mucinous Differentiation A conjunctival squamous intraepithelial neoplasia characterized by the presence of dysplastic squamous cells with intracytoplasmic mucin. MONDO:0003453 MONDO:0979715 conjunctival squamous intraepithelial neoplasia 2 NCIT:C212845 MONDO:equivalentTo Conjunctival Squamous Intraepithelial Neoplasia 2 A conjunctival squamous intraepithelial neoplasia characterized by the presence of dysplasia that involves the lower two-thirds of epithelial thickness. MONDO:0003453 MONDO:0979716 conjunctival squamous cell carcinoma in situ NCIT:C212849 MONDO:equivalentTo Conjunctival Squamous Cell Carcinoma In Situ A conjunctival squamous cell neoplasm characterized by the presence of dysplasia that involves the entire epithelium (full thickness) without surface epithelial maturation. The basement membrane is intact. MONDO:0006173,MONDO:0004693 MONDO:0979717 keratoacanthoma NCIT:C212871 MONDO:equivalentTo Keratoacanthoma A dome-shaped, rapidly growing neoplasm composed of well differentiated squamous cells. It almost always affects the skin and usually occurs on sun-exposed areas of the body, most often the head, neck, and limbs. Rare cases have been reported in extracutaneous sites including the conjunctiva, subungual space, and vulva. It is considered a variant of well-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma with distinct clinical behavior. MONDO:0005096 MONDO:0979718 essential thrombocythemia with recurrent thrombosis NCIT:C212978 MONDO:equivalentTo Essential Thrombocythemia with Recurrent Thrombosis Essential thrombocythemia associated with the repeated formation of blood clots due to the underlying disorder. MONDO:0005029 MONDO:0979719 von hippel lindau syndrome-associated clear cell renal cell carcinoma NCIT:C213036 MONDO:equivalentTo Von Hippel Lindau Syndrome-Associated Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma A clear cell renal cell carcinoma that develops in a patient with Von Hippel Lindau syndrome. Renal involvement in Von Hippel Lindau syndrome is characterized by multiple, bilateral, and recurring tumors. MONDO:0018492 MONDO:0979720 von hippel lindau syndrome-associated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor NCIT:C213039 MONDO:equivalentTo Von Hippel Lindau Syndrome-Associated Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumor A pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor that develops in a patient with Von Hippel Lindau syndrome. Most often, there are multiple non-functional tumors. MONDO:0019954 MONDO:0979721 refractory malignant neoplasm of unknown primary NCIT:C213042 MONDO:equivalentTo Refractory Malignant Neoplasm of Unknown Primary A metastatic malignant neoplasm of unknown primary that is resistant to treatment. MONDO:0858997,MONDO:0036501 MONDO:0979722 men1-associated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor NCIT:C213055 MONDO:equivalentTo MEN1-Associated Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumor A pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor that develops in a patient with multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1). The incidence of pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors in patients with MEN1 ranges between 30-80% in various studies. MONDO:0019954 MONDO:0979723 compound nevus NCIT:C213114 MONDO:equivalentTo Compound Nevus A nevus that arises from the skin or conjunctiva and is characterized by the presence of nevus cells within the epithelium and in the dermis (skin) or substantia propria (conjunctiva). MONDO:0005073 MONDO:0979724 balloon cell nevus NCIT:C213115 MONDO:equivalentTo Balloon Cell Nevus A melanocytic nevus that arises from the skin or conjunctiva and is characterized by the presence of large melanocytes with clear, foamy, or finely vacuolated cytoplasm. MONDO:0005073 MONDO:0979725 spitz nevus NCIT:C213118 MONDO:equivalentTo Spitz Nevus A benign melanocytic neoplasm that occurs in the skin and rarely the conjunctiva and is characterized by a proliferation of large epithelioid and/or spindled melanocytes. MONDO:0005073 MONDO:0979726 dysplastic nevus NCIT:C213198 MONDO:equivalentTo Dysplastic Nevus A slightly raised pigmented melanocytic lesion with irregular borders characterized by the presence of atypical melanocytes. The differential diagnosis from melanoma may be difficult and patients are at an increased risk for the development of melanoma. MONDO:0005073 MONDO:0979727 junctional nevus NCIT:C213199 MONDO:equivalentTo Junctional Nevus A melanocytic nevus that arises from the skin or conjunctiva. In the skin, it is characterized by the presence of a junctional proliferation of nevus cells without involvement of the dermis. In the conjunctiva, it is characterized by an intraepithelial proliferation of nevus cells. MONDO:0005073 MONDO:0979728 conjunctival amelanotic melanoma NCIT:C213201 MONDO:equivalentTo Conjunctival Amelanotic Melanoma A melanoma that arises from the conjunctiva and is characterized by the absence of melanin pigment in the melanoma cells. MONDO:0002096,MONDO:0002971 MONDO:0979729 conjunctival mixed epithelioid and spindle cell melanoma NCIT:C213202 MONDO:equivalentTo Conjunctival Mixed Epithelioid and Spindle Cell Melanoma A melanoma that arises from the conjunctiva and is characterized by the presence of malignant large epithelioid melanocytes and malignant spindle-shaped melanocytes. MONDO:0006749,MONDO:0002096 MONDO:0979730 metastatic carcinoma in the lymph nodes NCIT:C213275 MONDO:equivalentTo Metastatic Carcinoma in the Lymph Nodes A carcinoma that has spread to the lymph nodes. MONDO:0005438,MONDO:0024879 MONDO:0979731 metastatic carcinoma in the colon NCIT:C213276 MONDO:equivalentTo Metastatic Carcinoma in the Colon A carcinoma that has spread to the colon from another anatomic site. MONDO:0041447,MONDO:0024879 MONDO:0979732 sigmoid colon neoplasm NCIT:C213279 MONDO:equivalentTo Sigmoid Colon Neoplasm A benign or malignant neoplasm that affects the sigmoid colon. MONDO:0005401 MONDO:0979733 papillary urothelial carcinoma NCIT:C213296 MONDO:equivalentTo Papillary Urothelial Carcinoma An invasive or non-invasive urothelial carcinoma exhibiting papillary growth. MONDO:0040679,MONDO:0006509,MONDO:0003443 MONDO:0979734 border of tongue squamous cell carcinoma NCIT:C213305 MONDO:equivalentTo Border of Tongue Squamous Cell Carcinoma A squamous cell carcinoma that arises from the border of the tongue. MONDO:0000500 MONDO:0979737 lung acantholytic squamous cell carcinoma NCIT:C213321 MONDO:equivalentTo Lung Acantholytic Squamous Cell Carcinoma A rare variant of squamous cell carcinoma of the lung characterized by cellular discohesion of the tumor cells that results in the formation of pseudolumina resembling glandular structures. MONDO:0003487,MONDO:0005097 MONDO:0979738 head and neck cutaneous carcinoma NCIT:C213333 MONDO:equivalentTo Head and Neck Cutaneous Carcinoma A carcinoma that arises from the skin of the head and neck. MONDO:0002656,MONDO:0002038 MONDO:0979739 adult hepatoblastoma NCIT:C213350 MONDO:equivalentTo Adult Hepatoblastoma A rare hepatoblastoma that occurs during adulthood. MONDO:0018666 MONDO:0979740 hepatic flexure neoplasm NCIT:C213372 MONDO:equivalentTo Hepatic Flexure Neoplasm A benign or malignant neoplasm that affects the hepatic flexure. MONDO:0005401 MONDO:0979741 pancreatic ductal intestinal-type adenocarcinoma NCIT:C213375 MONDO:equivalentTo Pancreatic Ductal Intestinal-Type Adenocarcinoma A rare pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma characterized by the presence of intestinal-type malignant epithelial cells resembling colonic adenocarcinoma. MONDO:0005184,MONDO:0006254 MONDO:0979742 high grade serous adenocarcinoma NCIT:C213446 MONDO:equivalentTo High Grade Serous Adenocarcinoma A rapidly growing serous adenocarcinoma that arises from the ovary, fallopian tube, or peritoneum. It is characterized by the presence of high-grade cytologic features and frequent mitotic figures. MONDO:0005278 MONDO:0979743 low grade serous adenocarcinoma NCIT:C213448 MONDO:equivalentTo Low Grade Serous Adenocarcinoma A serous adenocarcinoma that arises from the ovary or the peritoneum and is characterized by low-grade histopathologic features. MONDO:0005278 MONDO:0979744 intraductal carcinoma NCIT:C213452 MONDO:equivalentTo Intraductal Carcinoma A carcinoma that arises from the epithelial lining of a duct and has not invaded the surrounding stroma. MONDO:0004993 MONDO:0979745 head and neck adenosquamous carcinoma NCIT:C213477 MONDO:equivalentTo Head and Neck Adenosquamous Carcinoma An adenosquamous carcinoma that arises from the head and neck region. MONDO:0006074,MONDO:0002038 MONDO:0979746 colorectal hepatoid adenocarcinoma NCIT:C213479 MONDO:equivalentTo Colorectal Hepatoid Adenocarcinoma A rare and aggressive extrahepatic carcinoma that morphologically and immunophenotypically resembles hepatocellular carcinoma and arises from the colon or rectum. MONDO:0006243,MONDO:0005008 MONDO:0979747 mediastinal melanoma NCIT:C213491 MONDO:equivalentTo Mediastinal Melanoma An exceedingly rare melanoma that arises from the mediastinum. MONDO:0006320,MONDO:0005843 MONDO:0979748 temporal bone paraganglioma NCIT:C213492 MONDO:equivalentTo Temporal Bone Paraganglioma A paraganglioma that arises from the temporal bone. MONDO:0006239 MONDO:0979749 maxillary bone paraganglioma NCIT:C213493 MONDO:equivalentTo Maxillary Bone Paraganglioma A paraganglioma that arises from the maxillary bone. MONDO:0006239 MONDO:0979750 parotid gland melanoma NCIT:C213517 MONDO:equivalentTo Parotid Gland Melanoma An exceedingly rare melanoma that arises from the parotid gland. The vast majority of melanomas affecting the parotid gland are metastatic lesions. MONDO:0006320,MONDO:0004700 MONDO:0979751 lung undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma NCIT:C213523 MONDO:equivalentTo Lung Undifferentiated Pleomorphic Sarcoma An exceedingly rare undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma that arises from the lung. In the vast majority of cases lung involvement is due to metastasis from another anatomic site. MONDO:0002426,MONDO:0002142 MONDO:0979752 lung desmoplastic small round cell tumor NCIT:C213527 MONDO:equivalentTo Lung Desmoplastic Small Round Cell Tumor An exceedingly rare desmoplastic small round cell tumor that arises from the lung. MONDO:0019373,MONDO:0002426 MONDO:0979753 lung liposarcoma NCIT:C213538 MONDO:equivalentTo Lung Liposarcoma An exceedingly rare liposarcoma that arises from the lung. MONDO:0002426,MONDO:0005060 MONDO:0979754 retroperitoneal liposarcoma NCIT:C213540 MONDO:equivalentTo Retroperitoneal Liposarcoma A liposarcoma that arises from the retroperitoneum. It is the most common soft tissue sarcoma of the retroperitoneum. MONDO:0001501,MONDO:0005060 MONDO:0979755 liver liposarcoma NCIT:C213546 MONDO:equivalentTo Liver Liposarcoma An exceedingly rare liposarcoma that arises from the liver. MONDO:0002397,MONDO:0005060 MONDO:0979756 colon gastrointestinal stromal tumor NCIT:C213590 MONDO:equivalentTo Colon Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor A gastrointestinal stromal tumor that arises from the colon. MONDO:0005401,MONDO:0006159 MONDO:0979757 synovial sarcoma of nerve NCIT:C213591 MONDO:equivalentTo Synovial Sarcoma of Nerve A rare synovial sarcoma that arises from a nerve. MONDO:0021089,MONDO:0010434 MONDO:0979758 lung ewing sarcoma NCIT:C213633 MONDO:equivalentTo Lung Ewing Sarcoma An exceedingly rare Ewing sarcoma that arises from the lung. MONDO:0018270,MONDO:0002426 MONDO:0979759 female reproductive system lymphoma NCIT:C213738 MONDO:equivalentTo Female Reproductive System Lymphoma A rare lymphoma that arises from the female reproductive system. There is no AJCC staging system for other rare tumors of the lung. (AJCC 9th Ed.) MONDO:0005138 MONDO:0981125 thymus epithelial neoplasm by ajcc v9 stage NCIT:C222524 MONDO:equivalentTo Thymus Epithelial Neoplasm by AJCC v9 Stage A term that refers to the staging of a thymus epithelial neoplasm, following the rules of the TNM AJCC v9 classification system. This staging system applies to all thymus epithelial neoplasms, including thymomas and thymus carcinomas, and thymus neuroendocrine neoplasms. (AJCC 9th Ed.) MONDO:0018079 MONDO:0981126 endometrial adenocarcinoma, not otherwise specified NCIT:C222632 MONDO:equivalentTo Endometrial Adenocarcinoma, Not Otherwise Specified An adenocarcinoma that arises from the endometrium and is characterized by the absence of specific morphological features to allow further classification. MONDO:0005461 MONDO:0981127 her2-ultralow breast carcinoma NCIT:C222693 MONDO:equivalentTo HER2-Ultralow Breast Carcinoma A breast adenocarcinoma defined by very low expression of HER2. MONDO:0004988 MONDO:0981128 pharyngeal carcinoma by ajcc v9 stage NCIT:C222757 MONDO:equivalentTo Pharyngeal Carcinoma by AJCC v9 Stage A term that refers to the staging of pharyngeal carcinoma according to the American Joint Committee on Cancer, 9th edition. MONDO:0021345 MONDO:0981129 mesothelioma in situ NCIT:C223046 MONDO:equivalentTo Mesothelioma In Situ A preinvasive mesothelial neoplasm that arises on the surfaces that contain mesothelial lining (pleura, peritoneum, pericardium, and tunica vaginalis) and is characterized by the proliferation of mesothelial cells in a single layer without invasion into underlying tissues. It requires demonstration of nuclear BAP1 loss or cytoplasmic MTAP loss by immunohistochemistry, or CDKN2A homozygous deletion by FISH. It is a precursor lesion to malignant mesothelioma, it most often affects the pleura, and usually occurs in older adults. MONDO:0006292 MONDO:0981130 lung oncocytoma NCIT:C223176 MONDO:equivalentTo Lung Oncocytoma An extremely rare benign epithelial neoplasm that arises from submucosal salivary glands in the respiratory tract and is characterized by the presence of oncocytic cells with abundant eosinophilic and granular cytoplasm. MONDO:0010795,MONDO:0002732 MONDO:0981131 lung schwannoma NCIT:C223177 MONDO:equivalentTo Lung Schwannoma An extremely rare schwannoma that arises from the lung. MONDO:0002732,MONDO:0004820 MONDO:0981132 lung non-small cell carcinoma, not otherwise specified NCIT:C223188 MONDO:equivalentTo Lung Non-Small Cell Carcinoma, Not Otherwise Specified A term that is only used for lung cytopathological specimens and small biopsies in which there are features of poorly differentiated carcinoma present, but there is no morphological and immunocytochemical evidence of adenocarcinoma or squamous cell carcinoma differentiation. MONDO:0005233 MONDO:0981133 primary pulmonary salivary gland-type tumor NCIT:C223194 MONDO:equivalentTo Primary Pulmonary Salivary Gland-Type Tumor A group of rare neoplasms that arise from the bronchial submucosal glands and resemble salivary gland tumors. The majority of these tumors are carcinomas, usually mucoepidermoid carcinoma, adenoid cystic carcinoma, and epithelial-myoepithelial carcinoma. Benign tumors include pleomorphic adenoma and sialadenoma papilliferum. MONDO:0021117 MONDO:0981134 gastroesophageal junction neuroendocrine neoplasm NCIT:C223236 MONDO:equivalentTo Gastroesophageal Junction Neuroendocrine Neoplasm A neoplasm with neuroendocrine differentiation that arises from the gastroesophageal junction. It includes neuroendocrine carcinomas (poorly differentiated neuroendocrine neoplasms) and extremely rare neuroendocrine tumors (well-differentiated neuroendocrine neoplasms). MONDO:0024503 MONDO:0981135 pancreatic schwannoma NCIT:C223347 MONDO:equivalentTo Pancreatic Schwannoma An extremely rare schwannoma that arises from the pancreas. It is usually located in the head of the pancreas. MONDO:0021470,MONDO:0004820 MONDO:0981136 pancreatic lymphangioma NCIT:C223348 MONDO:equivalentTo Pancreatic Lymphangioma A rare lymphangioma that arises from the pancreas. It occurs in women more often than men and is usually located in the distal pancreas. MONDO:0021470,MONDO:0021726 MONDO:0981137 pancreatic granular cell tumor NCIT:C223350 MONDO:equivalentTo Pancreatic Granular Cell Tumor An extremely rare, usually benign granular cell tumor that arises from the pancreas. MONDO:0021076,MONDO:0006235 MONDO:0981138 pancreatic neurofibroma NCIT:C223351 MONDO:equivalentTo Pancreatic Neurofibroma An extremely rare neurofibroma that arises from the pancreas. MONDO:0021470,MONDO:0016755 MONDO:0981139 pancreaticobiliary neoplasm NCIT:C223357 MONDO:equivalentTo Pancreaticobiliary Neoplasm A benign, premalignant, or malignant neoplasm that affects the pancreas or biliary tract (gallbladder and bile ducts). MONDO:0021223 MONDO:0981140 hormone receptor-positive invasive breast lobular carcinoma NCIT:C223362 MONDO:equivalentTo Hormone Receptor-Positive Invasive Breast Lobular Carcinoma An invasive breast lobular carcinoma that is positive for hormone receptors. MONDO:0005051 MONDO:0981141 her2-negative invasive breast lobular carcinoma NCIT:C223367 MONDO:equivalentTo HER2-Negative Invasive Breast Lobular Carcinoma An invasive breast lobular carcinoma that is negative for the expression of the HER2 receptor. MONDO:0005051,MONDO:0000618 MONDO:0981142 triple-negative invasive breast lobular carcinoma NCIT:C223369 MONDO:equivalentTo Triple-Negative Invasive Breast Lobular Carcinoma An invasive breast lobular carcinoma that is negative for expression of estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR), and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2). MONDO:0005051,MONDO:0005494 MONDO:0981143 pancreatic ewing sarcoma NCIT:C223537 MONDO:equivalentTo Pancreatic Ewing Sarcoma A rare Ewing sarcoma that arises from the pancreas. MONDO:0018270,MONDO:0002117 MONDO:0981144 pancreatic germ cell tumor NCIT:C223542 MONDO:equivalentTo Pancreatic Germ Cell Tumor An extremely rare extragonadal germ cell tumor that arises from the pancreas. MONDO:0018201,MONDO:0021040 MONDO:0981145 oligometastatic malignant neoplasm NCIT:C223845 MONDO:equivalentTo Oligometastatic Malignant Neoplasm A malignant neoplasm that has metastasized to a limited number of sites. MONDO:0024880 MONDO:0981146 female reproductive system carcinosarcoma NCIT:C223955 MONDO:equivalentTo Female Reproductive System Carcinosarcoma An aggressive, high-grade malignant tumor that arises from the female reproductive system and is composed of carcinomatous and sarcomatous elements. The vast majority of cases are malignant mixed mesodermal (Mullerian) tumors that originate from the Mullerian ducts. Exceedingly rare cases that arise from mesonephric remnants have also been described. MONDO:0001416,MONDO:0002928 MONDO:0981147 salivary gland cancer by ajcc v9 stage NCIT:C224096 MONDO:equivalentTo Salivary Gland Cancer by AJCC v9 Stage A term that refers to the staging of salivary gland cancer according to the American Joint Committee on Cancer, 9th edition. This staging applies to cancers arising in the major and minor salivary glands. The following histopathologic types are not included in this staging system: squamous cell carcinoma, neuroendocrine carcinoma, basosquamous cell carcinoma, lymphoma, sarcoma, and mucosal melanoma. (from AJCC 9th Ed.) MONDO:0000521 MONDO:0981148 platinum-sensitive malignant female reproductive system neoplasm NCIT:C224161 MONDO:equivalentTo Platinum-Sensitive Malignant Female Reproductive System Neoplasm A malignant female reproductive system neoplasm that has a documented response to platinum-based chemotherapy. MONDO:0001416 MONDO:0981149 malignant brachial plexus neoplasm NCIT:C224692 MONDO:equivalentTo Malignant Brachial Plexus Neoplasm A primary or metastatic malignant neoplasm that affects the brachial plexus. The most common primary malignant neoplasm of the brachial plexus is malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor. Metastatic malignant neoplasms that affect the brachial plexus most commonly originate from the lung or breast. Patients may present with a palpable mass and sensory and/or motor deficits or may be asymptomatic. MONDO:0003700,MONDO:0021089 MONDO:0981150 esophageal squamous papillomatosis NCIT:C224827 MONDO:equivalentTo Esophageal Squamous Papillomatosis An exceedingly rare condition characterized by the presence of numerous squamous papillomas arising from the mucosal surface of the esophagus. MONDO:0004267,MONDO:0004827 MONDO:0981151 esophageal undifferentiated carcinoma, not otherwise specified NCIT:C224859 MONDO:equivalentTo Esophageal Undifferentiated Carcinoma, Not Otherwise Specified An esophageal undifferentiated carcinoma characterized by the absence of SWI/SNF complex deficiency. MONDO:0018481 MONDO:0981152 esophageal carcinoma, swi/snf deficient NCIT:C224860 MONDO:equivalentTo Esophageal Carcinoma, SWI/SNF Deficient An esophageal undifferentiated carcinoma characterized by SWI/SNF complex deficiency that results from the loss of subunit ARID1A, SMARCA2, SMARCA4, or SMARCB1. MONDO:0018481 MONDO:0981153 esophageal lymphoepithelioma-like carcinoma NCIT:C224861 MONDO:equivalentTo Esophageal Lymphoepithelioma-Like Carcinoma An extremely rare esophageal undifferentiated carcinoma characterized by the presence of large epithelioid cells, a syncytial growth pattern, and a lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate. MONDO:0003572,MONDO:0018481 MONDO:0981154 paramedullary disease in multiple myeloma NCIT:C224864 MONDO:equivalentTo Paramedullary Disease in Multiple Myeloma Infiltration of soft tissue adjacent to cortical bone by malignant (clonal) plasma cells in patients with history of multiple myeloma. Unlike extramedullary disease in multiple myeloma, which is detached from bone, paramedullary disease in multiple myeloma develops via disruption of cortical bone and grows into adjacent tissue. MONDO:0009693 MONDO:0981155 acute myeloid leukemia with genetic abnormalities NCIT:C224900 MONDO:equivalentTo Acute Myeloid Leukemia with Genetic Abnormalities A term that refers to acute myeloid leukemias characterized by the presence of recurrent genetic abnormalities or other non-specific genetic abnormalities. MONDO:0018874 MONDO:0981156 childhood acute myeloid leukemia with recurrent genetic abnormalities NCIT:C224907 MONDO:equivalentTo Childhood Acute Myeloid Leukemia with Recurrent Genetic Abnormalities Acute myeloid leukemias with recurrent genetic abnormalities occurring in children. MONDO:0004996,MONDO:0017893 MONDO:0981157 peripheral t-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified with cytotoxic phenotype NCIT:C225039 MONDO:equivalentTo Peripheral T-Cell Lymphoma, Not Otherwise Specified with Cytotoxic Phenotype A peripheral T-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified characterized by the presence of a cytotoxic immunophenotype. MONDO:0004964 MONDO:0981158 extramedullary disease in acute myeloid leukemia NCIT:C225325 MONDO:equivalentTo Extramedullary Disease in Acute Myeloid Leukemia Infiltration of organs and soft tissues by malignant (clonal) myeloid blasts in patients with history of acute myeloid leukemia. MONDO:0018874 MONDO:0981159 gestational trophoblastic tumor by figo stage NCIT:C6390 MONDO:equivalentTo Gestational Trophoblastic Tumor by FIGO Stage A term that refers to the staging of gestational trophoblastic tumors according to the FIGO (Fédération Internationale de Gynécologie et d'Obstétrique) staging system. MONDO:0018944 MONDO:0981160 pericardial adenomatoid tumor NCIT:C92187 MONDO:equivalentTo Pericardial Adenomatoid Tumor An exceedingly rare adenomatoid tumor that arises from the pericardium. MONDO:0021514,MONDO:0004230

Source name: DO

Source description: The Disease Ontology has been developed as a standardized ontology for human disease with the purpose of providing the biomedical community with consistent, reusable and sustainable descriptions of human disease terms, phenotype characteristics and related medical vocabulary disease concepts through collaborative efforts of biomedical researchers, coordinated by the University of Maryland School of Medicine, Institute for Genome Sciences (https://disease-ontology.org/).

Homepage: https://disease-ontology.org/

Comments about this source: None

docs.title: MONDO - ORDO Alignment
docs.text:
Source name: Orphanet Rare Disease Ontology

Source description: "The Orphanet Rare Disease ontology (ORDO) was jointly developed by Orphanet and the EBI to provide a structured vocabulary for rare diseases capturing relationships between diseases, genes and other relevant features which will form a useful resource for the computational analysis of rare diseases (https://www.orphadata.org)."

Homepage: http://www.orphadata.org/

Comments about this source: ORDO is not really OWL in the strict sense. For example, disease 2 gene relationships follow the 'some, some' logic (a disease may have basis in the mutation of one of these), while the OWL interpretation of these axioms is that the disease has basis in the mutation of all of them. Example: ramona wartz disease can have a mutation in any (not all) of the genes recorded in ORDO. This is why great care needs to be taking interpreting diesease 2 gene relationships during ingest!

docs.title: Curation Instructions
docs.text:
• For every orphanet class that is associated with more than a gene, we should check if that gene is associated with a subclass. If so, we could have a gap. We may want to use the d2g links for gap filling.
  • ORDO d2g relations follow some-some logic rather than OWL's all-some semantics. It is important not to import them blindly, see comments.
